youtube.title: A POLITICAL AGENDA
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by Ro Edge and Jackson Fowler for a pre-election roundtable covering Nicky Hager’s latest book, National’s crime campaign, the changing role of social media, Parliament’s declining standards and proposed local government reforms. They also discuss the growing interest in strategic voting under MMP and what it could mean as voters head to the ballot box. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: DON BRASH & MATT ROBSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by Don Brash and Matthew Robson for a wide-ranging discussion on Nicky Hager’s latest book and the importance of allowing competing interpretations to be heard. They debate claims made about the Taxpayers’ Union, Winston Peters’ approach to foreign policy, New Zealand’s relationship with major powers and whether recent planning and tax reforms will deliver the changes promised. Check out last week's episode of Don Brash & Matt Robson | Shooting the Political Breeze For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: JODIE BRUNING
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Jodie Bruning of Physicians and Scientists for Global Responsibility about the research underpinning NZ First's new health policy, which she helped draft. Jodie explains the science linking ultra-processed carbohydrates to widespread metabolic decline, defends the policy against accusations of lobby-group influence and outlines proposals to remove GST from whole foods, tax sugary drinks and revive a nutritious school lunch programme modelled on France's. Discover more at PSGR For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: DAME ELIZABETH RATA
youtube.summary: Simon O'Connor speaks with Dame Elizabeth Rata about her 40-part YouTube series documenting the history of New Zealand's education system, built from primary sources on Maori and Pakeha efforts to establish shared national institutions. Elizabeth argues against presentism and postmodern relativism, explains what a knowledge-rich curriculum actually means, and traces the decline she sees in education since the 1970s toward indigenisation and the rejection of universal knowledge. Dame Elizabeth's lecture series: History of New Zealand Education | New episodes every Friday at 10.30am For more on this visit Elizabeth Rata’s website, or find her on YouTube

youtube.title: PETER WILLIAMS ON POLITICS
youtube.summary: Peter Williams returns from overseas to find New Zealand politics largely unchanged, dismissing Nicky Hager's new book as media noise that won't shift the election. He argues supermarket break-up proposals from across the political spectrum are economically illiterate, pointing instead to fuel taxes as a driver of grocery prices, and makes the case for right-leaning voters to back ACT or New Zealand First to strengthen a future coalition, floating NZ First's Craig Stobo as his pick for Finance Minister. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart examines the latest parliamentary controversy involving Te Pāti Māori co-leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer, offensive language in the House, and the standards of behaviour expected from elected representatives. She also looks at Speaker Maureen Pugh’s handling of the incident and asks whether declining respect for Parliament is putting the political system itself under strain. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X

youtube.title: MICHAEL ARBON
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon examines Australia’s proposed digital duty of care, questioning whether giving government greater power over online platforms could have unintended consequences. He highlights existing user-choice features on X, concerns raised by the US government over algorithmic suppression of lawful expression, and potential impacts on free speech, journalism and businesses. With the proposal still at exposure-draft stage, Michael considers what could be at stake if it reaches Parliament. Discover more from Michael on Facebook and X
